title: Import Strategy: Strict Jensen + Strict Convex rpow
content: The crucial imports are Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Jensen (for StrictConvexOn.map_sum_lt — the strict Jensen inequality on Finset sums) and Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.SpecificFunctions.Basic (for strictConvexOn_rpow — strict convexity of x ↦ xᵖ for p > 1). The local prerequisite Proofs.AmgmInequalityOQ03 supplies the weightedPowerMean definition that this entry's main theorem characterizes.
mathContext: Strict Jensen: $f$ strictly convex, weights $w_i > 0$ summing to 1, points $p_i$ not all equal $\implies f(\sum w_i p_i) < \sum w_i f(p_i)$

title: Nonemptiness from Sum-One Constraint
content: A small but essential auxiliary: positive weights summing to 1 must come from a nonempty index set, since an empty Finset has Σ = 0 ≠ 1. Used downstream to extract a witness index for the 'all equal' case. The proof is by case split on s.eq_empty_or_nonempty: if empty, simp closes the contradiction with hw'.
mathContext: $\forall i \in s, w_i > 0 \text{ and } \sum_{i \in s} w_i = 1 \implies s \ne \emptyset$

title: Positivity of Weighted Power Sum
content: Both A := Σ wᵢ zᵢʳ and B := Σ wᵢ zᵢᵗ must be strictly positive — needed to take rpow with possibly negative exponents and to use rpow_mul with nonneg base. Proof structure: each summand wᵢ zᵢʳ > 0 by mul_pos applied to (hw i hi) and rpow_pos_of_pos (hz i hi); Finset.sum_pos requires nonemptiness from the prior lemma.
mathContext: $w_i > 0,\ z_i > 0,\ s \ne \emptyset \implies \sum_{i \in s} w_i z_i^r > 0$ for any $r \in \mathbb{R}$
prerequisites: positivity preservation under multiplication and sum

title: The Critical Inequality t/r > 1
content: This is the single load-bearing step that connects the hypothesis r < t to the strict convexity of x^(t/r). The proof is by a clean calculation: 1 = r·r⁻¹ < t·r⁻¹ = t/r, using mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right with the positivity of r⁻¹. Without t/r > 1 the function x ↦ x^(t/r) would not be strictly convex (it would be linear at t/r = 1, concave below), and the entire strict-Jensen approach would collapse.
mathContext: $0 < r < t \implies 1 < t/r$ — and only then is $x \mapsto x^{t/r}$ strictly convex on $[0,\infty)$

title: Bridging A^(t/r) and B via Power Rule
content: The identity (zᵢʳ)^(t/r) = zᵢᵗ is what lets us recognize Σ wᵢ (zᵢʳ)^(t/r) (the right-hand side of strict Jensen applied to f(x) = x^(t/r)) as Σ wᵢ zᵢᵗ = B. Proof uses Real.rpow_mul (nonneg base) plus a field_simp on r·(t/r) = t. The companion rewrite hB_rw expresses B as Σ wᵢ (zᵢʳ)^(t/r), staging the Jensen application.
mathContext: $(z_i^r)^{t/r} = z_i^{r \cdot (t/r)} = z_i^t$ via $\operatorname{Real.rpow\_mul}$ on nonnegative bases

title: Step 1: M_r = M_t Reduces to A^(t/r) = B
content: The first step of the forward direction algebraically eliminates the outer 1/r and 1/t exponents. Starting from M_r = M_t (i.e. A^(1/r) = B^(1/t)), raise both sides to power t: (A^(1/r))^t = (B^(1/t))^t. The left becomes A^((1/r)·t) = A^(t/r) by rpow_mul, the right becomes B^((1/t)·t) = B^1 = B. This is the essential algebraic move — it converts the equality of two roots into an equality of one rpow expression with a sum.

title: Strict Jensen Forces Contradiction
content: The mathematical heart of the proof: assume by contradiction that some zⱼʳ ≠ zₖʳ. Apply StrictConvexOn.map_sum_lt with f(x) = x^(t/r) (strictly convex by strictConvexOn_rpow since t/r > 1). The hypothesis ⟨j, hj, k, hk, hjkr⟩ provides the 'non-constant' witness. Strict Jensen then gives f(Σ wᵢ zᵢʳ) < Σ wᵢ f(zᵢʳ), i.e., A^(t/r) < B. This contradicts step1 (which forced A^(t/r) = B), so the assumption was false and z_jʳ = z_kʳ for all j, k. Crucially, this avoids the equality-case analysis of Jensen entirely — strict Jensen + non-constant input directly yields strict inequality.
mathContext: $f(x) = x^{t/r}$ strictly convex, $\exists j, k:\ z_j^r \ne z_k^r \implies A^{t/r} = f\Bigl(\sum w_i z_i^r\Bigr) < \sum w_i f(z_i^r) = B$ — contradicts $A^{t/r} = B$

title: Final Step: rpow Injectivity
content: Having established z_jʳ = z_kʳ for all j, k via strict Jensen, the conclusion z_j = z_k follows by injectivity of x ↦ x^r on [0, ∞) (Real.rpow_left_inj). The injectivity requires r ≠ 0, supplied by ne_of_gt hr. This is a small but essential step: strict convexity of f only gives equality of the inputs to f (i.e., zᵢʳ values), and converting to equality of zᵢ requires the inverse function.
mathContext: $z_i, z_j \ge 0,\ r \ne 0,\ z_i^r = z_j^r \iff z_i = z_j$

title: Converse: All Equal ⟹ M_r = M_t
content: The easy direction: if all zᵢ = z_{i₀} (the witness from nonempty_of_pos_sum_one), then A = z_{i₀}^r · Σwᵢ = z_{i₀}^r · 1 = z_{i₀}^r, and similarly B = z_{i₀}^t. The outer 1/r and 1/t powers then collapse: A^(1/r) = (z_{i₀}^r)^(1/r) = z_{i₀}^(r·(1/r)) = z_{i₀}^1 = z_{i₀}, and B^(1/t) = z_{i₀} likewise. The key Mathlib lemmas are rpow_mul (on nonneg base) and rpow_one. This direction needs no convexity at all — pure algebraic substitution.
mathContext: $z_i \equiv c \implies A = c^r,\ B = c^t \implies A^{1/r} = c = B^{1/t} \implies M_r = M_t$

title: Corollary: AM = QM iff All Equal
content: Specialization to r = 1 (arithmetic mean) and t = 2 (quadratic mean = root-mean-square). The classical statement 'AM = QM iff zᵢ all equal' follows immediately by instantiating the main theorem with one_pos, two_pos, one_lt_two. This is the most pedagogically familiar form of the equality condition — it appears in textbooks under headings like 'Cauchy's mean inequality' and 'sharpness of the AM-QM inequality.'
mathContext: $\dfrac{\sum w_i z_i}{1} = \sqrt{\sum w_i z_i^2}\ \iff\ z_1 = \cdots = z_n$

title: Corollary: Strict AM < QM under Variation
content: Combines the weak inequality AM ≤ QM (from power_mean_monotone_pos in the AmgmInequalityOQ03 prerequisite) with the equality characterization (from am_eq_qm_iff_all_eq) via lt_of_le_of_ne. If even one pair zⱼ ≠ zₖ, equality fails, so the weak ≤ becomes strict <. This is the classical 'variance is nonnegative' fact dressed up: in fact, QM² - AM² is exactly the variance Var(z) under the weighting w, so AM < QM is precisely Var(z) > 0 when z is not constant.
mathContext: $\text{some } z_j \ne z_k \implies \operatorname{AM}(z, w) < \operatorname{QM}(z, w)$, equivalent to $\operatorname{Var}_w(z) > 0$
